That would be the same mechanism as this afternoon's top-view streaks.

found.q1_replace_live: Ember: yes. It is better than the live frame and worse nowhere that a visitor sees. The arm is parked off the record, the label is blank, the white parts at the arm and post feet are gone, the grain is halved and now matches the Tropos, and the shadow in front of the deck now carries red. The ground is identical to the live frame. Its red is no deeper than live: the front face is slightly less red and the platter's white band is gone. Fog: not as it stands. It fixes the same faults (arm, lettering, white feet, grain), and the clear deck now lets light into its shadow (10-13 L* lighter in front). But it adds a new fault visible at page size: the right side face glows white at L* 99, brighter than the floor at 93, with hard-edged gray stripes. It is the brightest thing in the frame and reads as an edge-lit bar or pasted white blocks. It also breaks the house rule (a), which is why the README chose 'none' for Fog; this frame uses a twentieth. Re-render Fog with the edge lamp at none, or with whatever stops the light reaching the far edge, then check that face against the floor. If the lettering on the live label has to go today, v3 Fog is the lesser fault, but it is not a pass.
found.q2_other_six: Not yet the same way. The ground, camera, shadow, contact and grain are ready to reuse unchanged. Two things carry over badly. First, the edge-lamp light travels through the slab and comes out at the far (right) side face, with hard shadows of the holes. At a twentieth in a clear deck that face already reaches L* 99 against a floor of 93. Dust (a tenth) and Acid and Ice (a third) pass much more light than Ember and will likely glow on that face as well, so in every tint measure the right side face (x 1070-1415, y 940-1270) against the floor beside it, not only the top and front medians. Second, the dark tints (Poison, Haze, Smoke) will probably read like Ember: dark brown-black fronts with colour only at the edges. Ember carries 6.6% strongly coloured deck pixels against the Tropos's 44%. The top's soft-sheen look and the seat discs seen through the front face will repeat in all six.
found.q3_reads_wrong: At visitor size: in Fog, the white glowing right side face with gray stripes and a stepped notch (blocking), and secondarily the white crescent in front of the arm base. found.q2_other_six: No, not with this scene as it stands. Three things carry over to every tint. First, the edges render as clear polished glass, not satin, so each tint's faces show only reflections and inner images instead of glowing in their own color. Second, an edge lamp can push a face to clipped white: in the pale tints (Ice at a third or a tenth, Dust, Acid) expect Fog's light-box face and a bright ring at the arm base. Third, the deep tints show only brown and black over the smoked base: Poison and Smoke would read nearly black, as Ember already reads brown. Haze, with no lamp, would show faces of pure reflection. Make the edges satin, keep every face below the floor, then test one pale tint (Ice) and one deep tint (Poison or Smoke) in this view before making the set.
found.q3_reads_wrong: Ember: the deck does not read as the same red as the Tropos Ember. It reads as a dark brown, oxblood or wood-like slab with one red corner and black or gray edges. A red light sits under the arm base like an LED. At full size, the polished top does not mirror the arm. Fog: the right side glows like a white light box; a white ring sits under the arm base; two shiny coin-like marks sit under the front edge. At full size the front edge looks like clear glass, where the product has satin edges.
